APA Write-Up for Chi-Square Test

apa_chi_writeup.Rd

Generates an APA-style paragraph reporting a chi-square test of independence.

Usage

apa_chi_writeup(
  chi_results_list,
  var1_name,
  var2_name,
  var1_labels = c("Level 1", "Level 2"),
  var2_labels = c("Level A", "Level B"),
  hypothesis_text = NULL,
  include_descriptives = TRUE,
  table_number = NULL
)

Arguments

chi_results_list

Output from chi_square_answers().

var1_name

Character string. Name of variable 1.

var2_name

Character string. Name of variable 2.

var1_labels

Character vector of length 2. Labels for var1 levels.

var2_labels

Character vector of length 2. Labels for var2 levels.

hypothesis_text

Character string or NULL. Custom hypothesis text.

include_descriptives

Logical. Include counts/percentages. Default TRUE.

table_number

Integer or NULL. Table reference number.

Value

A character string with APA write-up.

Examples

data(superman)
result <- chi_square_answers(superman, "clark_grp", "tomatometer")
#> Warning: Chi-squared approximation may be incorrect
writeup <- apa_chi_writeup(result,
  var1_name = "Height Group", var2_name = "Tomatometer",
  var1_labels = c("Under 6ft", "6ft+"),
  var2_labels = c("Rotten", "Fresh")
)
cat(writeup)
#> We hypothesized that Under 6ft would be equally likely to be Rotten or Fresh, whereas 6ft+ would show a different pattern. A chi-square test found no significant relationship between Height Group and Tomatometer, χ²(1) = 0.38, *p* = .537. Contrary to our hypothesis, participants from both Under 6ft (*n* = 2; 0%) and 6ft+ (*n* = 6; 16.67%) were equally likely to be Rotten.
